title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who came upon Azariah the son of Oded?
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God
questions.explanation: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:1.

questions.question: What did Azariah say to Asa?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is with you
questions.explanation: Azariah told Asa that the LORD is with him if he is with the LORD as per 2 Chronicles 15:2.

questions.question: For how long had Israel been without the true God?
questions.correctAnswer: A long season
questions.explanation: Israel had been without the true God for a long season according to 2 Chronicles 15:3.

questions.question: True or False: Azariah prophesied that God would not help Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Azariah indicated that God would be found if they sought Him, not that He would not help them, as seen in 2 Chronicles 15:2.

questions.question: What happened when the people turned to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They found peace
questions.explanation: When they turned to the LORD, He was found of them as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:4.

questions.question: True or False: In those times, there was peace for everyone who went out or came in.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: There was no peace for anyone during that time; great vexations were upon the inhabitants according to 2 Chronicles 15:5.

questions.question: What did Asa do after hearing the prophecy of Oded?
questions.correctAnswer: Put away idols
questions.explanation: Asa took courage and put away the abominable idols from the land of Judah and Benjamin as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 15:8.

questions.question: Which tribes gathered with Asa?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah and Benjamin
questions.explanation: Asa gathered all Judah and Benjamin as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:9.

questions.question: True or False: Asa renewed the altar of the LORD that was before the porch of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Asa renewed the altar of the LORD that was before the porch of the LORD as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:8.

questions.question: What did they offer to the LORD from the spoil?
options: Seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep
Two hundred oxen and three thousand sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep
questions.explanation: They offered seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep to the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 15:11.

questions.question: What covenant did they enter into?
options: To seek the LORD God with all their heart and soul
questions.correctAnswer: To seek the LORD God with all their heart and soul
questions.explanation: They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and soul as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:12.

questions.question: True or False: Asa allowed his mother to remain queen despite her idolatry.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Asa removed his mother from being queen because she made an idol, according to 2 Chronicles 15:16.

questions.question: How did the people react when they swore to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced
questions.explanation: All Judah rejoiced at the oath because they sought the LORD with their whole desire, as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:15.

questions.question: What was the state of war during the reign of Asa?
options: No more war until the thirty-fifth year
questions.correctAnswer: No more war until the thirty-fifth year
questions.explanation: There was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa, according to 2 Chronicles 15:19.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Asa do after hearing the prophecy of Oded the prophet?
options: He took courage and renewed the altar of the LORD
He sought counsel from his advisors
questions.correctAnswer: He took courage and renewed the altar of the LORD
questions.explanation: Asa took courage after hearing the prophecy and put away the abominable idols and renewed the altar of the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:8).

questions.question: What was the reason many from Israel joined Asa in Judah?
options: They were seeking refuge from war
They saw that the LORD his God was with him
They wanted to travel to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They saw that the LORD his God was with him
questions.explanation: Many from Israel joined Asa because they saw that the LORD his God was with him (2 Chronicles 15:9).

questions.question: In which month did the gathering of Judah and Benjamin take place?
questions.correctAnswer: Third month
questions.explanation: The gathering took place in the third month (2 Chronicles 15:10).

questions.question: How many oxen did they offer to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven hundred
questions.explanation: They offered seven hundred oxen to the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:11).

questions.question: What covenant did they enter into regarding seeking the LORD?
options: To seek the LORD only during war
To seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and soul
To seek the LORD only on the Sabbath
To seek the LORD when convenient
questions.correctAnswer: To seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and soul
questions.explanation: They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and soul (2 Chronicles 15:12).

questions.question: What was the consequence for those who would not seek the LORD God of Israel?
options: They should be put to death
questions.correctAnswer: They should be put to death
questions.explanation: The consequence for not seeking the LORD God of Israel was death, whether small or great, man or woman (2 Chronicles 15:13).

questions.question: They swore unto the LORD with what?
options: A loud voice, shouting, trumpets, and cornets
questions.correctAnswer: A loud voice, shouting, trumpets, and cornets
questions.explanation: They swore unto the LORD with a loud voice, shouting, trumpets, and cornets (2 Chronicles 15:14).

questions.question: True or False: Asa removed his mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Asa removed Maachah from being queen because she had made an idol in a grove (2 Chronicles 15:16).

questions.question: True or False: The high places were taken away out of Israel during Asa's reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The high places were not taken away out of Israel, although Asa's heart was perfect all his days (2 Chronicles 15:17).

questions.question: What did Asa bring into the house of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold and silver
questions.explanation: Asa brought into the house of God silver and gold, and vessels that he and his father had dedicated (2 Chronicles 15:18).

questions.question: How long did peace last during Asa's reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Until the thirty-fifth year
questions.explanation: There was no more war until the five and thirtieth year of Asa's reign (2 Chronicles 15:19).

questions.question: How does this passage teach us about obedience to God?
options: Obedience leads to peace and blessings
Obedience is only necessary for leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience leads to peace and blessings
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates that those who sought the LORD found Him and experienced rest and peace, showing the blessings that come from obedience (2 Chronicles 15:15).

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 15.

questions.question: What did Azariah the son of Oded say to Asa?
options: The LORD is with you if you seek Him
Peace will come without seeking God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is with you if you seek Him
questions.explanation: Azariah told Asa that 'The LORD is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you' (2 Chronicles 15:2).

questions.question: What were the consequences of forsaking the LORD according to Azariah?
questions.correctAnswer: He will forsake you
questions.explanation: Azariah warned Asa that 'if ye forsake him, he will forsake you' (2 Chronicles 15:2).

questions.question: What significant action did Asa take after hearing Azariah's prophecy?
options: He removed idols from Judah and Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: He removed idols from Judah and Benjamin
questions.explanation: Asa took courage and 'put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin' (2 Chronicles 15:8).

questions.question: What was the offering made by Asa and the people of Judah?
options: Seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep
questions.explanation: They offered 'seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep' to the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:11).

questions.question: What covenant did Asa and the people enter into?
options: To seek the LORD God of their fathers
questions.correctAnswer: To seek the LORD God of their fathers
questions.explanation: They entered into a covenant 'to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul' (2 Chronicles 15:12).

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 15:13, what was the penalty for not seeking the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Death
questions.explanation: The covenant stated that 'whosoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel should be put to death' (2 Chronicles 15:13).

questions.question: What action did Asa take regarding his mother, Maachah?
options: He removed her from being queen
He made her an idol maker
questions.correctAnswer: He removed her from being queen
questions.explanation: Asa 'removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove' (2 Chronicles 15:16).

questions.question: What was Asa's heart condition throughout his reign?
options: It was perfect all his days
questions.correctAnswer: It was perfect all his days
questions.explanation: Despite the high places remaining, 'the heart of Asa was perfect all his days' (2 Chronicles 15:17).

questions.question: What did Asa bring into the house of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold and silver
questions.explanation: He brought into the house of God 'the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels' (2 Chronicles 15:18).

questions.question: What was the state of war during the reign of Asa?
options: No war until the thirty-fifth year
questions.correctAnswer: No war until the thirty-fifth year
questions.explanation: There was 'no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa' (2 Chronicles 15:19).

questions.question: True or False: Asa's actions led to rest for Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The chapter concludes that 'he was found of them: and the LORD gave them rest round about' (2 Chronicles 15:15).

questions.question: True or False: Asa did not care about the idols in Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Asa actively removed idols, showing he cared about the worship of the true God (2 Chronicles 15:16).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of seeking God to find Him?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 6:33
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:33 states 'But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you,' echoing the theme of seeking God (2 Chronicles 15:2).

questions.question: Which Old Testament chapter parallels the removal of idols as seen in Asa's actions?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Kings 18
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18 discusses King Hezekiah's similar action of removing idols, paralleling Asa's reforms (2 Chronicles 15:8).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'covenant' (berith) signify in the context of Asa's covenant?
questions.correctAnswer: Agreement
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'berith' signifies an agreement, which is evident in the covenant to seek the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:12).

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 15:2 teach about the relationship between God and His people?
options: God is with them when they seek Him
God is indifferent to their actions
God only helps those who are strong
questions.correctAnswer: God is with them when they seek Him
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes that the LORD is with the people as long as they seek Him, highlighting the conditional nature of God's presence in relation to human action (2 Chronicles 15:2).

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 15:3, what has Israel been without for a long season?
options: True God, teaching priest, and law
questions.correctAnswer: True God, teaching priest, and law
questions.explanation: This verse indicates that Israel lacked the true God, a teaching priest, and law, which are essential for spiritual guidance and community order (2 Chronicles 15:3).

questions.question: What action did Asa take after hearing the prophecy of Oded the prophet as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 15:8?
options: Renewed the altar of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Renewed the altar of the LORD
questions.explanation: Asa took courage and renewed the altar of the LORD, demonstrating his commitment to restoring true worship in Judah (2 Chronicles 15:8).

questions.question: What was the offer made to the LORD by the people of Judah and Benjamin as noted in 2 Chronicles 15:11?
options: Seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep
Five hundred goats and five thousand lambs
One thousand bulls and one thousand rams
Ten thousand birds and ten thousand fish
questions.correctAnswer: Seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep
questions.explanation: The people offered seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep to the LORD as a sign of their dedication and gratitude (2 Chronicles 15:11).

questions.question: What covenant did the people of Judah enter into as stated in 2 Chronicles 15:12?
options: To seek the LORD God with half their heart
To seek the LORD God with all their heart and soul
To uphold the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: To seek the LORD God with all their heart and soul
questions.explanation: The people covenanted to seek the LORD God with all their heart and soul, which signifies total commitment (2 Chronicles 15:12).

questions.question: What was the consequence for anyone who would not seek the LORD God of Israel according to 2 Chronicles 15:13?
options: They should be put to death
questions.correctAnswer: They should be put to death
questions.explanation: The verse states that anyone who did not seek the LORD was to be put to death, highlighting the seriousness of their covenant commitment (2 Chronicles 15:13).

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 15:15 reveal about the people's response to their covenant with God?
options: They rejoiced and sought Him with their whole desire
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced and sought Him with their whole desire
questions.explanation: The text shows that all Judah rejoiced at the oath and sought the LORD with their whole desire, indicating a sincere commitment to their covenant (2 Chronicles 15:15).

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 15:16, what action did Asa take concerning his mother Maachah?
options: He removed her from being queen
He built her a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: He removed her from being queen
questions.explanation: Asa removed Maachah from being queen because she had made an idol in a grove, demonstrating his commitment to purging idolatry from Judah (2 Chronicles 15:16).

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 15:19 imply about the reign of Asa?
options: There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of his reign
He expanded the kingdom through war
He faced rebellion from his own people
questions.correctAnswer: There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of his reign
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that Asa experienced a time of peace, with no war until the thirty-fifth year of his reign, reflecting God's favor on his leadership (2 Chronicles 15:19).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 15:4 regarding His response to Israel's troubles?
questions.correctAnswer: His mercy
questions.explanation: The verse shows that when the people turned to the LORD in their trouble, He was found of them, illustrating God's merciful nature in response to repentance (2 Chronicles 15:4).

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 15:7 encourage the people to do, and what is the promise attached to it?
options: Be strong; their work will be rewarded
Pray earnestly; they will find peace
Repent fully; they will be forgiven
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong; their work will be rewarded
questions.explanation: This verse encourages strength and reassures the people that their efforts in seeking the Lord will be rewarded, linking diligence with divine favor (2 Chronicles 15:7).

questions.question: In light of 2 Chronicles 15:9, what was the significance of the gathering of Judah, Benjamin, and the strangers?
options: It marked the beginning of a new kingdom
It demonstrated unity and acknowledgement of God's presence
It indicated a time of war
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrated unity and acknowledgement of God's presence
questions.explanation: The gathering represents a unified response to God's presence and leadership, showing that many from Israel recognized the LORD was with Asa (2 Chronicles 15:9).

questions.question: What theological truth can be derived from combining 2 Chronicles 15:2 and 15:4?
options: God is always present regardless of human action
Seeking God leads to finding Him
God is indifferent to the people’s distress
Idolatry does not affect God’s presence
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking God leads to finding Him
questions.explanation: These verses collectively teach that if the people seek the LORD, they will find Him, indicating a relationship built on pursuit and response (2 Chronicles 15:2, 15:4).

questions.question: What combined message do 2 Chronicles 15:12 and 15:14 convey about the community's commitment to God?
options: They joyfully entered into a covenant to seek God
questions.correctAnswer: They joyfully entered into a covenant to seek God
questions.explanation: These verses indicate that the community solemnly covenanted to seek God with excitement and commitment, showcasing their collective desire for divine relationship (2 Chronicles 15:12, 15:14).

questions.question: Skeptics claim that the Old Testament presents a vengeful God. What does 2 Chronicles 15:4 teach about God's character?
options: God is responsive to the repentance of His people
God operates without regard to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God is responsive to the repentance of His people
questions.explanation: This verse illustrates that when the people turned to the LORD in their trouble, He was found of them, showing His grace and readiness to respond to sincere repentance (2 Chronicles 15:4).
